newsitem.title: ITALY: Leading Italian mobster seized in Sicily.
newsitem.headline: Leading Italian mobster seized in Sicily.

text.p: Pietro Aglieri, believed to be one of the most senior Mafia godfathers in Italy, has been arrested, Italian news agency Ansa reported on Friday.
Ansa, quoting Palermo police chief Antonino Manganelli, said two suspected Mafia hitmen were also arrested, dealing a further blow to organised crime on the southern Italian island of Sicily.

Aglieri was one of the three most wanted Mafiosi in Italy and some investigators believe he may have taken charge of Cosa Nostra following the capture in 1993 of Salvatore "The Beast" Riina. There were no immediate details of Aglieri's arrest.

In separate police operations earlier on Friday, 12 suspected Mafia members were seized in the southern heel of Italy, and six alleged mobsters were arrested in the Sicilian city of Catania on drug-related charges.

The old Italian Mafia leadership was effectively dismantled after the spectacular mob murders of magistrates Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino in 1992, with Riina, his second in command Leoluca Bagarella and feared gangster Giovanni Brusca all now behind bars.
However Italian police reported that the Mafia had retrenched, with Aglieri taking a leading role in re-shaping the depleted organisation.
